feature_name: VPC Flow Logs support for RDMA flows over Converged Ethernet
summary: VPC Flow Logs now captures RDMA traffic, including GPU-to-GPU RDMA flows over Converged Ethernet.
extended_definition: VPC Flow Logs now captures RDMA traffic, including GPU-to-GPU RDMA flows over Converged Ethernet.

supporting_pages.title: VPC Flow Logs \_|\_ Virtual Private Cloud \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: For RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE), only outbound flows are sampled.

For example, you can analyze the network flows for the following: Traffic between regions and zones Traffic to specific countries on the internet Traffic to on-premises and other cloud networks Top talkers in the network, including VMs, serverless endpoints, VLAN attachments, and Cloud VPN tunnels Network forensics You can use VPC Flow Logs for network forensics.

For example, if an incident occurs, you can examine the following: Which IP addresses have communicated with each other and when Which IPs are compromised by analyzing all the incoming and outgoing network flows Supported configurations You can enable VPC Flow Logs at the organization and project levels.

supporting_pages.title: "About VPC Flow Logs records \_|\_ Virtual Private Cloud \_|\_ Google Cloud\
evidence_snippets: 3 If VPC Flow Logs is configured at the organization level, by default, log records for cross-project flows include details about both sides of the flow.

Populated for all flows. src port int32 Source port: Populated for TCP and UDP flows Not populated for ICMP, ESP, GRE, and RDMA flows dest port int32 Destination port: Populated for TCP and UDP flows Not populated for ICMP, ESP, GRE, and RDMA flows GatewayDetails field format Field Type Description project id string Google Cloud project ID of the gateway location string Region of the gateway name string Name of the gateway type string Type of the gateway.

If you select custom metadata, you can specify the metadata fields that you want to include by the parent field, such as src vpc , or by their full names, such as src vpc.project id When new metadata fields are added to the record format, they're excluded from the flow logs unless they're within a parent field that you have specified to include.

supporting_pages.title: "Flow Analyzer overview \_|\_ Network Intelligence Center - Flow Analyzer\
evidence_snippets: In Flow Analyzer, you can do the following: Query logs reported by VPC Flow Logs Use SQL filters to refine your queries Sort query results by total traffic, aggregate packets, or latency View traffic for a specific time period View the top five flows with the highest traffic or latency, for the selected time period View resources with the highest traffic or latency, for the selected time period View traffic details for specific source and destination pairs in your query results How it works VPC Flow Logs samples packets in your VPC network to generate flow logs, which can be stored in Cloud Logging or routed to supported destinations, such as BigQuery or a third-party platform through Pub/Sub.
Flow Analyzer lets you quickly and efficiently understand your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) traffic flows without the need to write complex SQL queries for analyzing VPC Flow Logs.
For more information, see the VPC Flow Logs overview .
